text:
B: Hello, can you hear me? I'm Alison.
A: Yes, hello. I'm Hetal. Sorry, I was just moving the laptop.
B: Oh, don't worry, I've been doing that all afternoon. I saw your sewing machine in your picture. Do you do much sewing?
A: Yes, I'm a tailor. Alterations. But my shop closed, so I'm looking for work now.
B: Oh, I'm sorry. That's a worry. How long has it been?
A: Eighteen months, erm, about. I'm applying, department stores, uniform companies. But the interviews, I get so nervous. I forget everything.
B: Oh, I know that feeling. I trained as a nurse in my thirties, and my interview, I was shaking. I'd been in a building society before that, I thought, they'll laugh at me.
A: But you got it?
B: I did, and I've been a nurse twenty-odd years now. Erm, what helped me was writing down two or three things I was proud of. Just little things, so I had something to say.
A: I write notes also, for the Jobcentre phone calls. Before every call.
B: Well, there you are. That's sensible, not silly. What would you write, if it was an interview tomorrow?
A: Erm. Nine years, I never lost a garment. And I see if a hem is two millimetres off.
B: That's brilliant. Say that, exactly like that. They'll remember it.
A: Okay. Thank you. Today also, the other people give me ideas. One lady said curtain workrooms, another said check charity shops for a second machine.
B: Oh, see, everyone's looking out for you. That's nice, isn't it?
A: Yes. Everyone is very kind today. Sorry, what about you, you sew?
B: Only mending. Buttons, hems. Badly, I expect you'd say.
A: (laughs) No, no. Mending is good. Most people throw away.
B: I sing in a choir as well, Tuesdays. And I have a cat, Biscuit. And my tomatoes, in a little greenhouse, they've done ever so well this year.
A: I have a tulsi plant on my window. For a long time it didn't grow, now finally it's doing well.
B: Tulsi, is that basil?
A: Holy basil, yes. For the mandir, for prayers. My mum is very happy it's growing.
B: Oh, that's lovely. Do you live with your mum?
A: No, alone. My parents are in Harrow. I go on Sundays.
B: I live on my own too. Since my divorce. It's nice, but the evenings can be a bit quiet, can't they?
A: Yes. Sometimes very quiet. I put old Hindi songs on.
B: I put the radio on, so it's the same thing really. Sorry, I don't know if that's —
